newsitem.title: UK: Mark off slightly as market focuses on Ecofin.
newsitem.headline: Mark off slightly as market focuses on Ecofin.

text.p: The mark slipped slightly on most crosses in morning Europe as EU finance ministers chorused assurances that European monetary union was on track.
The ministers, at an Ecofin meeting in Luxembourg, dismissed any talk of delaying EMU, and said France's new government had shown a clear commitment to the project.

Talk of a punctual start to EMU usually depresses the mark as it fans fears that it will be swallowed up into a weaker currency. Those concerns have been stoked by the new French administration's stated desire to see a broad group of countries
A key focus was the budget stability pact -- designed to enforce fiscal discipline after EMU begins -- which the French Socialists questioned during the election campaign.
French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said he would give his views late Monday morning on the pact, which is due to be sealed at the Amsterdam summit on June 16-17.
Strauss-Kahn said Sunday that he could not see how anyone could have doubted France's commitment to launching EMU in 1999.
"He's certainly making the sort of noises people will be looking for if EMU's going to go ahead on time," said David Brickman, European economist at Yamaichi International here.

The mark eased to lows of 983.35 Italian lire and 3.3734 French francs in early Europe from late Friday's levels of 986.00/30 and 3.3763/66 respectively. But it had climbed back to 985.70/90 and 3.3763/68 by 0813 GMT.
Some analysts were unconvinced by the rhetoric out of Luxembourg so far.
"I think it's what you'd expect them to say. The key focus is likely to be on the Franco-German summit at the end of the week," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International.
Concern that EMU would be weak, or could be delayed or even collapse, would keep investors shy of European assets, he said.
"A lot of investors are looking at other markets rather than pushing their money into a very uncertain environment," said Edmonds.
Julian Jessop, chief European economist at Nikko Europe, felt talk of EMU delay was premature.
"I think the political will behind the project is strong enough to tide them over the next few meetings, but obviously the risks of (EMU) break-up are now higher than ever.
"The mark, I think, is going to remain firm on the European crosses but weak against the dollar," Jessop said.
The Irish pound firmed against the mark and sterling after the weekend election which brought victory to a centre-right alliance but left it two seats short of parliamentary majority.
The punt stood at 2.5855/25 marks and 0.9190/15 sterling at 0830 GMT versus 2.5690/5740 and 0.9133 at Friday's close here.
Data out of Spain showed unemployment fell to 13.26 percent in May from April's 13.61. The rate was 14.36 in May 1996.
The peseta changed hands at 84.61/63 per mark compared to 84.57/59 late on Friday.
-- Abigail Levene, London Newsroom +44-171-542-8968
